title: WORKSHEET 47
subject: Purpose: So that / to / In order to / In Case
subjectVi: Ngữ pháp bài 47: Purpose: So that / to / In order to / In Case

sections.instruction: Combine the sentences using the words in brackets: (Example: Jane gave up smoking because she wanted to save money. (in order to) → Jane gave up smoking in order to save money.)

questions.prompt: I came here so that I could see you. (in order to)
acceptedAnswers: I came here in order to see you.

questions.prompt: We put up a fence. We want to prevent the rabbit from escaping. (in order to / so that)
acceptedAnswers: We put up a fence in order to prevent the rabbit from escaping.
We put up a fence to prevent the rabbit from escaping.
We put up a fence so that the rabbit can't escape.
We put up a fence so that the rabbit won't escape.
questions.explanation: purpose: in order to / so that

questions.prompt: She went shopping so she could buy herself a television. (to)
acceptedAnswers: She went shopping to buy herself a television.

questions.prompt: I put the food in the fridge because I wanted it to get cold. (in order to)
acceptedAnswers: I put the food in the fridge in order for it to get cold.
I put the food in the fridge in order to make it cold.
I put the food in the fridge in order to get it cold.
I put the food in the fridge in order to keep it cold.
questions.explanation: in order (for + object) to + base verb

questions.prompt: Jane saved money. She wanted to buy a present for Harry. (in order to)
acceptedAnswers: Jane saved money in order to buy a present for Harry.
Jane saved money in order to buy Harry a present.

questions.prompt: Harry left early because he didn't want to miss the bus. (in order not to)
acceptedAnswers: Harry left early in order not to miss the bus.
questions.explanation: in order not to + base verb

questions.prompt: They will let the students use calculators in the exam. They don't want them to spend a lot of time. (so that)
acceptedAnswers: They will let the students use calculators in the exam so that they won't spend a lot of time.
They will let the students use calculators in the exam so that they don't spend a lot of time.

questions.prompt: The teacher tested the students. She wanted to see if they remembered the things they had learnt. (in order to)
acceptedAnswers: The teacher tested the students in order to see if they remembered the things they had learnt.
The teacher tested the students in order to see if they remembered the things they had learned.

questions.prompt: She didn't leave her son home alone. She thought he might have an accident. (in case)
acceptedAnswers: She didn't leave her son home alone in case he had an accident.
She didn't leave her son home alone in case he might have an accident.
She didn't leave her son home alone in case he should have an accident.

questions.prompt: He tried to hide the broken vase. He didn't want to be punished. (so that)
acceptedAnswers: He tried to hide the broken vase so that he wouldn't be punished.
He tried to hide the broken vase so that he didn't get punished.

questions.prompt: She wants to sign a contract. She doesn't want them to change their minds. (in case)
acceptedAnswers: She wants to sign a contract in case they change their minds.

questions.prompt: I turned up the radio. I wanted to listen to the news. (so that)
acceptedAnswers: I turned up the radio so that I could listen to the news.
I turned up the radio so that I could hear the news.

questions.prompt: Sue lowered the volume on the TV set. She didn't want to disturb her roommate. (so that)
acceptedAnswers: Sue lowered the volume on the TV set so that she wouldn't disturb her roommate.
Sue lowered the volume on the TV set so that she didn't disturb her roommate.

questions.prompt: I'll be in my office until late this evening. You may need to get in touch with me. (in case)
acceptedAnswers: I'll be in my office until late this evening in case you need to get in touch with me.

questions.prompt: I'll give you my phone number. You may need to speak to me. (in case)
acceptedAnswers: I'll give you my phone number in case you need to speak to me.

questions.prompt: Tom marked his friend's birthday on the calendar. He thought he might forget it. (in case)
acceptedAnswers: Tom marked his friend's birthday on the calendar in case he forgot it.
Tom marked his friend's birthday on the calendar in case he might forget it.
Tom marked his friend's birthday on the calendar in case he forgot.

sections.instruction: Combine each pair of sentences using “IN CASE”:

questions.prompt: You'd better take a sweater. It might get cold.
acceptedAnswers: You'd better take a sweater in case it gets cold.

questions.prompt: We'd better book a table. The restaurant might be full.
acceptedAnswers: We'd better book a table in case the restaurant is full.

questions.prompt: You ought to insure your jewellery. It might get stolen.
acceptedAnswers: You ought to insure your jewellery in case it gets stolen.
You ought to insure your jewelry in case it gets stolen.
You ought to insure your jewellery in case it is stolen.

questions.prompt: I'm watching this saucepan. The water might boil over.
acceptedAnswers: I'm watching this saucepan in case the water boils over.

questions.prompt: I'll leave you my phone number. You might want to contact me.
acceptedAnswers: I'll leave you my phone number in case you want to contact me.

sections.instruction: Join the sentences using the words in brackets:

questions.prompt: He tried to find a car park. He wanted to park his car. (in order to)
acceptedAnswers: He tried to find a car park in order to park his car.

questions.prompt: Mrs. Brown hid the ball. She didn't want Bill to play football. (so that)
acceptedAnswers: Mrs. Brown hid the ball so that Bill couldn't play football.
Mrs. Brown hid the ball so that Bill wouldn't play football.

questions.prompt: They got up early. They didn't want to miss the bus. (in case)
acceptedAnswers: They got up early in case they missed the bus.
They got up early in case they should miss the bus.

questions.prompt: Mary is wearing glasses. She wants to see better. (so that)
acceptedAnswers: Mary is wearing glasses so that she can see better.

questions.prompt: My father often takes his car to the mechanic. He doesn't want it to break down. (in case)
acceptedAnswers: My father often takes his car to the mechanic in case it breaks down.

questions.prompt: Molly is eating less bread. She doesn't want to put on weight. (in case)
acceptedAnswers: Molly is eating less bread in case she puts on weight.

questions.prompt: Sally usually wears a thick coat. She doesn't want to catch a cold. (in order not to)
acceptedAnswers: Sally usually wears a thick coat in order not to catch a cold.
questions.explanation: in order not to + base verb

questions.prompt: Mr. Short used a long ladder. He wanted to reach the high ceiling. (so that)
acceptedAnswers: Mr. Short used a long ladder so that he could reach the high ceiling.

questions.prompt: My father gave me extra money. He didn't want me to borrow any from my friends. (in case)
acceptedAnswers: My father gave me extra money in case I needed to borrow some from my friends.
My father gave me extra money in case I borrowed any from my friends.
My father gave me extra money in case I had to borrow some from my friends.

questions.prompt: Andrew's friends visited him. They wanted to congratulate him on his graduation. (in order to)
acceptedAnswers: Andrew's friends visited him in order to congratulate him on his graduation.

questions.prompt: I'm learning English. I want to get a better job. (to)

questions.prompt: The driver stopped. Then the children could cross the road. (so that)
acceptedAnswers: The driver stopped so that the children could cross the road.

questions.prompt: Tom put the cream in the fridge. That would keep it cool. (to)

questions.prompt: Mark is going to repair the roof. Then the rain won't come in. (so that)
acceptedAnswers: Mark is going to repair the roof so that the rain won't come in.
Mark is going to repair the roof so that the rain doesn't come in.

questions.prompt: We often switch off the heating. It saves money. (in order to)
acceptedAnswers: We often switch off the heating in order to save money.

questions.prompt: Pamela wore boots. Her feet wouldn't get wet. (so that)
